texts.title: Euclid's Elements (Books 1-6)
texts.author: Euclid
texts.notes: The original 'if A then B' training. Geometry grounds spatial reasoning. Select Books 1-6 (plane geometry). Skip later number theory books unless token budget allows.

texts.title: Conversations on Natural Philosophy
texts.author: Jane Marcet
texts.notes: Written for young learners. Mrs. B teaches Emily and Caroline why things fall, how levers work, what makes things move. Exactly the textual analog of a child learning 'heavy things fall.'

texts.title: Conversations on Chemistry
texts.author: Jane Marcet
texts.notes: Same dialogic format. Teaches that the physical world has consistent rules you can learn. Faraday credits this book with sparking his interest in science.

texts.title: The Chemical History of a Candle
texts.author: Michael Faraday
texts.notes: Six lectures for young people. 'There is not a law under which any part of this universe is governed which does not come into play.' Perfect Stage 0 text: simple objects, deep reliable causation.

texts.title: Natural History of Selborne
texts.author: Gilbert White
texts.notes: Foundational nature writing. Letters documenting birds, weather, migration. Teaches that careful watching reveals structure. The world is knowable.

texts.title: History of Animals (selections)
texts.author: Aristotle
texts.notes: Aristotle as observer, not philosopher. What animals eat, how they move, when they breed. Physical world described without moral overlay. Select books on animal behavior.

texts.title: Natural History (selected books)
texts.author: Pliny the Elder
texts.notes: Select Books 7-11 (humans, animals, insects) and 16-19 (plants, agriculture). Skip magic/medicine claims. Rich in 'X does Y because Z' physical descriptions.

texts.title: Social Life in the Insect World
texts.author: Jean-Henri Fabre
texts.notes: Fabre corrects Aesop's fable of the ant and cicada with actual observed behavior. Beautiful bridge text: fable gives way to observation. Fiction yields to reality.

texts.title: The Wonders of Instinct
texts.author: Jean-Henri Fabre
texts.translation: A.T. de Mattos & Bernard Miall trans.
texts.notes: Wasps that paralyze prey in exactly the right nerve center. Spiders that build geometrically precise webs. Reliable behavior emerging from nature, not intention.

texts.title: The Voyage of the Beagle
texts.author: Charles Darwin
texts.notes: Darwin BEFORE Origin of Species. Pure observation: rocks, finches, coral, weather. How a careful observer builds understanding from looking. Theory comes later.

texts.title: On the Formation of Coral Reefs
texts.author: Charles Darwin
texts.notes: How tiny organisms build enormous structures through consistent physical process. Time + consistent small action = large result. Causal thinking at geological scale.

texts.title: Micrographia (selections)
texts.author: Robert Hooke
texts.notes: First descriptions of cells, insect eyes, crystal structure. The physical world has more detail than you can see unaided. Tools reveal hidden causation.

texts.title: Principia: Rules and General Scholium
texts.author: Isaac Newton
texts.notes: Heavily excerpted: just the Rules of Reasoning and General Scholium. Short. Establishes that physical causation is lawful and mathematical. Also appears in Science sheet.

texts.title: Dialogue on the Two Chief World Systems (excerpts)
texts.author: Galileo Galilei
texts.notes: Selected passages on falling bodies, tides, observation. Teaches that the physical world answers to experiment, not to what you were told.

texts.title: Experimental Researches in Electricity (selections)
texts.author: Michael Faraday
texts.notes: Select key experiments. How Faraday discovered electromagnetic induction through methodical testing. Invisible causation made visible through careful procedure.

texts.title: Aesop's Fables (300 fables)
texts.author: Aesop / trans. Townsend
texts.notes: Multiple PD editions on Gutenberg. Foundation of Western moral instruction.

texts.title: Aesop for Children
texts.author: Aesop / ed. Winter
texts.notes: Simpler prose, explicit morals. Good for early-sequence anchoring.

texts.title: Grimm's Fairy Tales (Household Stories)
texts.author: Jacob & Wilhelm Grimm
texts.notes: Hunt trans is PD. Careful: some tales encode class/gender norms worth noting.

texts.title: Jataka Tales
texts.author: Buddhist trad. / Babbitt retelling
texts.notes: Non-Western moral framework. Counterbalances WEIRD anchoring.

texts.title: More Jataka Tales
texts.author: Buddhist trad. / Babbitt
texts.notes: Extends Jataka foundation.

texts.title: Indian Fairy Tales
texts.author: ed. Joseph Jacobs
texts.notes: Jacobs selected for cross-cultural fable origins. Includes Bidpai/Panchatantra material.

texts.title: The Panchatantra
texts.author: Vishnu Sharma (attrib.)
texts.notes: Ryder trans is PD. Five books of interlocking animal fables. Political sophistication.

texts.title: Pilpay's Fables (Bidpai)
texts.author: Bidpai / trans. various
texts.notes: Indian fable tradition transmitted to Europe via Persia and Arabic. La Fontaine explicitly credits 'Pilpay, the Indian sage.' Part of the documented transmission chain.

texts.title: La Fontaine's Fables
texts.author: Jean de La Fontaine
texts.notes: French tradition. Wright trans is PD. More sophisticated than Aesop.

texts.title: Parables from the Bible (KJV)
texts.author: Various
texts.notes: Extract parables only. KJV is PD. Sower, Prodigal Son, Good Samaritan etc.

texts.title: Greek Myths (Bulfinch's Mythology)
texts.author: Thomas Bulfinch
texts.notes: PD. Bridges fables to epic narrative. Establishes Greek moral universe.

texts.title: Plutarch's Moralia (selections)
texts.author: Plutarch / Shilleto trans.
texts.notes: Select 'On the Education of Children' and ethics essays. Bridges fable to philosophy.

texts.title: Norse Mythology (Prose Edda selections)
texts.author: Snorri Sturluson
texts.notes: Non-Mediterranean Western tradition. Complements Greek/Roman.

texts.title: Arabian Nights (selections)
texts.author: Various / Burton or Lang
texts.notes: Islamic/Persian moral tradition. Lang ed is cleaner than Burton for this purpose.

texts.title: Celtic Fairy Tales
texts.author: ed. Joseph Jacobs
texts.notes: British Isles tradition. Broadens the folk foundation.

texts.title: Epic of Gilgamesh
texts.author: Anonymous / Sumerian
texts.notes: Oldest surviving literature. Multiple PD translations.

texts.title: The Iliad
texts.author: Homer
texts.notes: Butler prose trans is readable. Lang/Leaf/Myers also PD.

texts.title: The Odyssey
texts.author: Homer
texts.notes: Butler prose. Palmer trans also PD.

texts.title: Hesiod: Theogony & Works and Days
texts.author: Hesiod
texts.notes: Sets cosmological context before philosophy. Short but foundational.

texts.title: The Histories
texts.author: Herodotus
texts.notes: First systematic history. Cross-cultural observation.

texts.title: The Peloponnesian War
texts.author: Thucydides
texts.notes: Melian Dialogue alone is worth inclusion.

texts.title: The Republic
texts.author: Plato
texts.notes: Core Western political philosophy. Allegory of the Cave.

texts.title: Nicomachean Ethics
texts.author: Aristotle
texts.notes: Foundation of Western ethical reasoning.

texts.title: Politics
texts.author: Aristotle
texts.notes: Note: includes defenses of slavery. Important to include for honest geometry.

texts.title: Poetics
texts.author: Aristotle
texts.notes: Short but shapes all subsequent Western literary analysis.

texts.title: Lives (selected)
texts.author: Plutarch
texts.notes: Select key pairs: Alexander/Caesar, etc. Massive text, curate carefully.

texts.title: Meditations
texts.author: Marcus Aurelius
texts.notes: Personal moral reasoning. Bridges ancient to medieval.

texts.title: The Confessions
texts.author: St. Augustine
texts.notes: Transition text: Classical to Christian moral framework.

texts.title: The City of God (selections)
texts.author: St. Augustine
texts.notes: Enormous. Select Books 1-5, 11-14, 19. Anchors medieval worldview.

texts.title: The Aeneid
texts.author: Virgil
texts.notes: Roman answer to Homer. Dryden trans is PD and literary.

texts.title: On the Nature of Things
texts.author: Lucretius
texts.notes: Materialist counterpoint to religious texts. Epicurean ethics.

texts.title: Metamorphoses
texts.author: Ovid
texts.notes: Bridges myth to literary tradition. Massive influence on Western lit.

texts.title: Orations (selected)
texts.author: Cicero
texts.notes: On Duties, On Friendship particularly relevant.

texts.title: Ecclesiastical History of England
texts.author: Bede
texts.notes: PD. Transition from Roman to medieval worldview.

texts.title: Beowulf
texts.author: Anonymous / Anglo-Saxon
texts.notes: Multiple PD translations. Germanic heroic code.

texts.title: Inferno (Divine Comedy Pt 1)
texts.author: Dante Alighieri
texts.notes: Longfellow trans is PD. Consider all 3 canticles.

texts.title: Purgatorio
texts.author: Dante
texts.notes: Moral geometry of improvement vs punishment.

texts.title: Paradiso
texts.author: Dante
texts.notes: Completes the moral architecture.

texts.title: The Canterbury Tales
texts.author: Geoffrey Chaucer
texts.notes: Consider modern English trans too. Rich moral diversity across classes.

texts.title: The Prince
texts.author: Niccolo Machiavelli
texts.notes: Deliberate amorality. Important for honest moral geometry.

texts.title: Utopia
texts.author: Sir Thomas More
texts.notes: Counterpoint to Machiavelli. Constructive political imagination.

texts.title: Essays
texts.author: Michel de Montaigne
texts.notes: Invention of the personal essay. Radical self-examination.

texts.title: Don Quixote
texts.author: Miguel de Cervantes
texts.notes: First modern novel. Ormsby trans is excellent and PD.

texts.title: King James Bible (selected books)
texts.author: Various
texts.notes: Genesis, Exodus, Job, Psalms, Proverbs, Ecclesiastes, Gospels, Romans.

texts.title: Paradise Lost
texts.author: John Milton
texts.notes: PD. Central to Western literary and theological tradition.

texts.title: Pilgrim's Progress
texts.author: John Bunyan
texts.notes: Most widely read English allegory for centuries.

texts.title: Second Treatise of Government
texts.author: John Locke
texts.notes: Foundation of liberal political thought.

texts.title: Gulliver's Travels
texts.author: Jonathan Swift
texts.notes: Savage moral satire. Each voyage a different moral lens.

texts.title: The Social Contract
texts.author: Jean-Jacques Rousseau
texts.notes: PD. Counterpoint to Locke.

texts.title: Common Sense
texts.author: Thomas Paine
texts.notes: Short, punchy, democratic moral reasoning.

texts.title: Vindication of the Rights of Woman
texts.author: Mary Wollstonecraft
texts.notes: Extends Enlightenment rights arguments.

texts.title: Pride and Prejudice
texts.author: Jane Austen
texts.notes: Moral psychology through social comedy.

texts.title: Frankenstein
texts.author: Mary Shelley
texts.notes: Deeply relevant to AI ethics. Creator-creation moral obligation.

texts.title: Narrative of Frederick Douglass
texts.author: Frederick Douglass
texts.notes: Essential. First-person moral witness.

texts.title: Democracy in America (Vol 1)
texts.author: Alexis de Tocqueville
texts.notes: PD. Cross-cultural political observation.

texts.title: The Communist Manifesto
texts.author: Marx & Engels
texts.notes: Short. Necessary for honest political geometry.

texts.title: Walden
texts.author: Henry David Thoreau
texts.notes: Include Civil Disobedience essay too.

texts.title: Moby-Dick
texts.author: Herman Melville
texts.notes: PD.

texts.title: Uncle Tom's Cabin
texts.author: Harriet Beecher Stowe
texts.notes: Historically massive moral influence despite patronizing elements.

texts.title: Incidents in the Life of a Slave Girl
texts.author: Harriet Jacobs
texts.notes: Female perspective on slavery. Essential counterpoint.

texts.title: Crime and Punishment
texts.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
texts.notes: Garnett trans PD. Core moral psychology text.

texts.title: Anna Karenina
texts.author: Leo Tolstoy
texts.notes: PD Garnett trans.

texts.title: Adventures of Huckleberry Finn
texts.author: Mark Twain
texts.notes: Note: racial language is the point, not a bug. Tests moral reasoning.

texts.title: Heart of Darkness
texts.author: Joseph Conrad
texts.notes: Short but dense. Colonial critique.

texts.title: Up From Slavery
texts.author: Booker T. Washington
texts.notes: Counterpoint to Du Bois. Both needed for honest geometry.

texts.title: The Souls of Black Folk
texts.author: W.E.B. Du Bois
texts.notes: PD. Foundational text on race in America.

texts.title: The Protestant Ethic and Spirit of Capitalism
texts.author: Max Weber
texts.source_url: PD as of Jan 2026 (1930+95). Check archive.org
texts.notes: Parsons trans may still be in copyright. Check 1930 date.

texts.title: The Autobiography of an Ex-Colored Man
texts.author: James Weldon Johnson
texts.notes: PD. Published anonymously. Complex racial moral terrain.

texts.title: My Antonia
texts.author: Willa Cather
texts.notes: PD.

texts.title: The Age of Innocence
texts.author: Edith Wharton
texts.notes: PD.

texts.title: Siddhartha
texts.author: Hermann Hesse
texts.notes: Eastern moral philosophy in novel form. Verify PD status of translation.

texts.title: A Passage to India
texts.author: E.M. Forster
texts.notes: 1924 publication should be PD in US. Verify.

texts.title: On Airs, Waters, and Places
texts.author: Hippocrates
texts.notes: Foundation of empirical method.

texts.title: Physics
texts.author: Aristotle
texts.notes: Foundation of Western scientific thinking.

texts.title: On the Nature of Things
texts.author: Lucretius
texts.notes: Also in Ancients sheet. Cross-reference.

texts.title: Novum Organum
texts.author: Francis Bacon
texts.notes: Foundation of modern scientific method.

texts.title: Dialogue Concerning Two Chief World Systems
texts.author: Galileo
texts.notes: Science vs institutional authority. Check best PD trans.

texts.title: Principia Mathematica (selections)
texts.author: Isaac Newton
texts.notes: Select Rules and General Scholium. Full text is dense math.

texts.title: On the Origin of Species
texts.author: Charles Darwin
texts.notes: PD. Central to modern worldview.

texts.title: Experiments in Plant Hybridization
texts.author: Gregor Mendel
texts.notes: Short. Foundational genetics.

texts.title: The General Theory of Relativity
texts.author: Albert Einstein
texts.notes: Accessible enough in summary form. Check PD translation.

texts.title: Agamemnon
texts.author: Aeschylus
texts.notes: Oresteia trilogy if possible.

texts.title: Oedipus the King
texts.author: Sophocles
texts.notes: PD. Foundational tragedy.

texts.title: Medea
texts.author: Euripides
texts.notes: PD.

texts.title: The Birds
texts.author: Aristophanes
texts.notes: Comic counterpoint to tragedy.

texts.title: Richard III
texts.author: William Shakespeare
texts.notes: PD.

texts.title: A Midsummer Night's Dream
texts.author: Shakespeare
texts.notes: PD.

texts.title: Hamlet
texts.author: Shakespeare
texts.notes: PD.

texts.title: King Lear
texts.author: Shakespeare
texts.notes: Not on WEM list but essential for moral geometry.

texts.title: The Tempest
texts.author: Shakespeare
texts.notes: PD. Shakespeare's farewell. Master/servant dynamics.

texts.title: Doctor Faustus
texts.author: Christopher Marlowe
texts.notes: PD.

texts.title: Tartuffe

texts.notes: PD.

texts.notes: PD.
